glasses3

glasses3 reads recordings from the Tobii Pro Glasses 3 wearable eye tracker into R. It works on the recording folder as it comes off the SD card, so Tobii Pro Lab is not needed.

The glasses store each data stream as gzipped JSON with one record per line (gazedata.gz, imudata.gz and eventdata.gz). glasses3 turns gaze, pupil diameter, IMU and sync port data into tibbles and reads the recording metadata. Samples are matched to sync port pulses, so the data can be cut into epochs around stimuli. Plots show pupil diameter over time and gaze position in the scene camera image.

Installation

glasses3 is not on CRAN yet. Install it from R-universe:

install.packages("glasses3", repos = c("https://mcanzi.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

Usage 

library(glasses3)

rec <- read_g3("path/to/recording")
rec
summary(rec)

plot_g3_pupil(rec)
plot_g3_gaze(rec, type = "density")

epochs <- g3_epochs(rec$gaze, rec$events, before = 0.5, after = 5)
plot_g3_pupil(epochs)
pupil <- g3_pupil_long(epochs)
binned <- g3_downsample(pupil, bin = 0.1)

gaze <- g3_gaze_angles(rec$gaze)

The package comes with a 30-second example recording, found with g3_example().

Several recordings

list_g3_recordings() finds every recording on an SD card or in any other folder. Pass its output to a reader and you get one tibble for all of them, with a recording column naming the folder each row comes from. The sync port functions match each recording to its own pulses, and the plots get one panel per recording.

recordings <- list_g3_recordings("path/to/sdcard")

gaze <- read_g3_gaze(recordings)
events <- read_g3_events(recordings)

epochs <- g3_epochs(gaze, events, before = 0.5, after = 5)
plot_g3_pupil(gaze, events)

The data come back as tibbles, so they work directly with dplyr and ggplot2, and grouped tibbles keep their groups.

Scope

glasses3 reads and organises the data. Lines that cannot be read, such as the cut-off end of an incomplete file, are skipped with a warning, and g3_fill_gaps() puts empty rows in their place. g3_downsample() averages the samples into time bins, for example before fitting generalised additive mixed models. The package leaves pupil preprocessing to other packages. Blink removal, interpolation and baseline correction are available in packages such as PupillometryR, gazer or eyeris.
